newsitem.title: NORWAY: Aker RGI mulls sale of Helly-Hansen stake.
newsitem.headline: Aker RGI mulls sale of Helly-Hansen stake.

text.p: Norwegian industrial holding company Aker RGI said on Tuesday it had begun negotiations for the possible sale of its 50 percent holding in clothing company Helly-Hansen AS for about 400 million crowns.
RGI acquired the stake for 125 million crowns in January 1995, before mergering with the Aker group.
In 1996 Helly-Hansen had total sales of 941 million crowns and an operating profit of 101 million crowns.
Aker RGI said a possible sale would give the company a gain on book value of 275 million crowns.
Food-based conglomerate Orkla ASA owns the other 50 percent stake of Helly-Hansen.

Aker RGI said the negotiations were based on an interest from the potential buyer to take over some of Orkla's shares. If the sale goes ahead, Orkla will retain about 30 percent of Helly-Hansen shares, it said.
